text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
OrderTakeout(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendsEatingTime(x) ::: x spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
NeedsMoney(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for college tuition.
Hannah ::: Hannah
MarysSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.

Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → NeedsMoney(x)) ::: If people work in student jobs on campus, then they need to earn money.
∀x (OrderTakeout(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people order takeout frequently, then they work in student jobs.
∀x (OrderTakeout(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ∧ Recipes(x))) ::: People order takeout or enjoy dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If they enjoy dining hall meals, then they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → SpendsEatingTime(x)) ::: If they enjoy dining hall meals, then they spend a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends.
Hannah ::: Hannah.
(WorksInStudentJobs(Hannah) ∧ (NeedsMoney(Hannah) → (¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∧ NeedsMoney(Hannah)))) ::: Hannah works in student jobs, and if she needs to earn money, then she is neither picky nor needs money.

Conclusion:
NeedsMoney(Hannah) ::: Hannah needs to earn money to help pay for her college tuition.
